sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The Phonology of Proto-Central Chadic: The reconstruction of the phonology and lexicon of Proto-Central Chadic, and the linguistic history of the Central Chadic languages. LOT Dissertation Series 375. Utrecht: LOT (PhD, Leiden).
sources.note: Comparative work; source table p. 13 reads 'Fali [fli] — Bata — none' (no description available); §3.3.1 Bata group (pp. 47-48) uses only Kraft's (1981) wordlist for 'Fali of Muchella'; p. 1 states the reconstruction does not include 'tone or stress'. Confirms the absence of any descriptive source for fli.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2011 (May). An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 3rd edition (draft). Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Entry 127 'Fali cluster' (p. 64).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Entry 127: 'Fali cluster', 2.A Fali of Mubi, Fali of Muchella; lects *Vin (Uroovin), *Huli (Urahuli), *Madzarin, *Ɓween (Uramɓween); Adamawa State, Mubi LGA; >20,000 (1990); 'Chadic: Biu-Mandara sub-branch A: Bata group'; 'Source(s) Blench (1992)' only — no phonology or grammar cited. Cross-references: Fali of Jilbu = Zizilivakan; Fali of Kiria/Mijilu = Kirya-Konzəl.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Anthony Ndamsai. 2009. An introduction to Kirya-Konzəl, a Central Chadic language of Eastern Nigeria. In Eva Rothmaler (ed.), Topics in Chadic Linguistics V, 75-85. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe.
sources.note: DIFFERENT LANGUOID (Kirya-Konzəl = 'Fali of Kirya/Mijilu', Glottolog kiry1234, Higi cluster). §3.3 Tones, p. 80: 'Fali appears to have two level tones, High and Low and rare downstep. Rising and falling tones occur but are comparatively rare.' No statement on stress. Table 3 (p. 78) lists the fli lects (Jilvu, Muchela/Madzarin, Vimtim/Uroviin, Bagera/Uramɓween, Bahuli/Urahuli) as 'Fali cluster' and says Kirya 'is not closely related to the Fali lects spoken east of Mubi'.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Anthony Ndamsai. 2007. A dictionary of Kirya and Konzəl in northeastern Nigeria (draft circulated for comment, printout Jos 6 Dec 2007). 53 pp.
sources.note: DIFFERENT LANGUOID (kiry1234). §3.3 Tones, p. 10, same two-tone statement as the offprint; nothing on stress. Notes that Kraft (1981:179ff.) gives a phonetically transcribed wordlist 'with a phonemic analysis by Martin Mould' that is 'misleading both in terms of tones and in relation to phonemes'.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page fali1285 (Fali; ISO fli; Chadic > Biu-Mandara > Gude; dialect Fali Muchella; subclassification per Hoskison 1983) and Wikipedia 'Fali of Mubi' (raw wikitext; cites only Blench's Atlas)
sources.note: Nothing. Glottolog counts 0 descriptive (grammar/sketch/phonology) references for fali1285; the earlier scan note ('only wordlists: Kraft 1981, Meek 1931') is confirmed. OLAC (403), Ethnologue (Cloudflare wall), SIL archive search (403) and HathiTrust (bot wall) could not be reached from our machine.

sources.citation: Meek, C. K. 1931. Tribal Studies in Northern Nigeria, vol. I. London: Kegan Paul, Trench, Trübner. Extract pp. 300-308 ('The Fali': A. Fali of Wuba District; B. Fali of Mubi District, pp. 303-308, with 'Fali (of Mubi) vocabulary')
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnographic notes plus a short numbered vocabulary in a rough phonetic transcription; the only pronunciation remark is a footnote on a lateral consonant. No mention of stress, accent or tone. Full volume on archive.org (tribalstudiesinn0001ckme) is lending-restricted; djvu text download refused (401).

sources.note: Not opened. Glottolog's own records show these are name-based ('autotranslated'/'computerized') assignments: the Cameroon ones concern the Adamawa Fali of northern Cameroon, Wente-Lukas concerns Bana, Lukas 1937 is a wordlist collection. None is a description of fli.
